subject.title: [Bug]: cron agentTurn returns before foreground Bash subprocess completes — long-running executors are killed mid-stream, leaving partial state and a placeholder digest

question: Should this cron foreground-Bash failure be fixed with a cron-specific pending-tool success blocker, or folded into the broader Claude CLI long-work lifecycle contract?
rationale: Source inspection supports the lifecycle gap, but the durable fix changes stable cron success semantics, announce delivery truth, Claude CLI live-session cleanup, and process-tree orphan safety.

options.title: Keep a cron-specific blocker
options.body: Require isolated cron to treat pending foreground native tool work as not finished, so it cannot record ok or announce placeholder output before the work completes or explicitly fails.

options.title: Fold into long-work lifecycle
options.body: Keep this issue open until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/102172 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101863 explicitly covers the cron green-status and announce-placeholder invariant.

options.title: Declare unsupported foreground longwork
options.body: Document or enforce that long foreground native Bash inside Claude CLI cron is unsupported and route users to durable command, exec/process, or detached task flows with clear diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Keep a cron-specific blocker
recommendation.body: Require isolated cron to treat pending foreground native tool work as not finished, so it cannot record ok or announce placeholder output before the work completes or explicitly fails.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus introduced the warm Claude CLI live-session path and is closest to the lifecycle contract being decided.
